question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English EIC commercial expansion — early factories and dates]
options: Surat — Formal factory established in 1613 under imperial Mughal farman
Masulipatnam — First English factory on the Coromandel coast established in 1611
Hariharpur (Odisha) — Early English factory in eastern India established in 1633
Calcutta — Fortified settlement of Fort William founded in 1619 by Job Charnock
wrong_fact: Calcutta (Fort William) was established much later, in 1690 (when Job Charnock secured the lease of Sutanuti, Gobindapur, and Kalikata), not in 1619. In 1619, English presence in Bengal did not exist.
explanation: The EIC established its Surat factory in 1613, Masulipatnam in 1611, and Hariharpur (Odisha) in 1633. Calcutta was founded by Job Charnock in 1690, and Fort William was constructed and fortified later in the 1690s, not 1619.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [East India Company expansion — geography of commercial hubs]
options: Patna (Bihar) — Inland commercial factory established in the mid-17th century for saltpetre and raw silk
Balasore (Odisha) — Coastal factory set up in 1633 to tap into the textile and saltpetre trade of the eastern coast
Broach (Gujarat) — Subsidiary factory established to collect cotton goods near Surat
Pondicherry — Primary English commercial headquarters in southern India established in 1674
wrong_fact: Pondicherry was the primary commercial headquarters of the French East India Company (established in 1674 by François Martin), not the English. The English headquarters in southern India was Fort St. George in Madras.
explanation: Patna, Balasore, and Broach were indeed important English commercial centers established during the 17th century. Pondicherry, however, was the administrative and commercial capital of the French EIC, whereas the English relied on Madras (Fort St. George) on the Coromandel coast.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [EIC's late 17th-century commercial expansion — Bengal presidency origins]
options: Sutanuti — One of the three villages (along with Gobindapur and Kalikata) acquired by the EIC in 1698 to form Calcutta
Hooghly — First EIC factory in Bengal established in 1651 by Bridgeman under permission from Shah Shuja
Kassim Bazar — Important silk-reeling factory centre in Bengal visited and developed by the EIC in the 1650s
Chandernagore — Fortified settlement established by Job Charnock in 1690 as the English capital of Bengal
wrong_fact: Chandernagore was a French fortified settlement (established in 1673), not English. The English settlement founded by Job Charnock in 1690 was Calcutta (Sutanuti).
explanation: The three villages of Sutanuti, Gobindapur, and Kalikata were purchased in 1698 to form Calcutta. The Hooghly factory was set up in 1651 with permission from Shah Shuja (governor of Bengal), and Kassim Bazar was a major silk center. Chandernagore was the rival French base in Bengal, while Calcutta was the English stronghold.
